chunks: Verily We gave to Moses the Book, but there was disagreement about it. Had the decree of your Lord (delaying it) not been issued the matter would have been settled between them. They are still suspicious of it and in doubt.

key_terms.كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ: A decree that preceded (God's decree of delay)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the disagreement regarding the Book given to Moses in Surah Hud?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the *ikhtilaf* (disagreement) among the Children of Israel regarding the Torah, often interpreted as a result of textual alteration (*tahrif*) or divergent interpretations of the Law. It underscores the divine wisdom of *al-hay'ah* (the decree of delay) in the eschatological judgment, allowing time for the emergence of the Ahl al-Bayt and the ultimate clarification of truth. This context serves as a precursor to the final judgment, emphasizing that current doubts are temporary until the decisive verdict is rendered.
